findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses bool fields (is_validated, is_sent) and a String status, allowing illegal states such as is_validated=false with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_sent=false. These invariants are invisible to the type system.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can construct or mutate PacketWorkflow into an inconsistent state (e.g. validated=false, sent=true) that violates domain invariants. No compiler enforcement prevents crossing from validated to sent without validation.
findings.fix: Replace is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, and status: String with a single PacketState enum typestate (e.g. Unvalidated, Validated, Sent { sent_at: EpochMs }). Remove status field entirely.

findings.problem: id uses raw String instead of a domain newtype. No parsing boundary or validation at construction.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, malformed IDs, and arbitrary-length strings all pass the type system. No invariant enforcement on id values.
findings.fix: Create a PacketId newtype struct with a fallible constructor that validates non-empty and bounded-length, returning a typed error.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms uses raw Option<u64> instead of a domain newtype for epoch timestamps.
findings.failure_mode: Zero, overflow-prone, or semantically invalid epoch values pass the type system. No domain constraint enforcement.
findings.fix: Create an EpochMs newtype wrapping u64 with a fallible constructor or derive from a validated source.

findings.problem: mark_sent does not check that the packet is in a validated state before marking as sent. It blindly transitions any PacketWorkflow to sent state.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated packet can be marked as sent, violating the domain workflow invariant that only validated packets may be sent.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept a PacketState enum and return Result<SentState, TransitionError>. The function should only accept Validated state and reject all others.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() allocation for the status string literal and mutates a raw struct in-place instead of returning a new immutable value.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every transition. Mutation pattern invites side effects in the core rather than pure functional transformation.
findings.fix: Remove the status field entirely (replaced by enum). Return a new typed state value instead of mutating in place.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub, exposing internal representation. No encapsulation of invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can directly mutate fields, bypassing all typestate transitions and constructors.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructors and transition methods that enforce invariants.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for any performance claims. The crate has no benchmarks/, benches/, or #[bench] code.
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims cannot be measured or validated. Any optimization decisions are cargo-cult.
findings.fix: Add a simple benchmark module or criterion tests if the crate has stated performance requirements.

missing_evidence: no benchmarks exist for any performance claims
no tests exist to validate typestate transitions
no allocation profiling evidence for .to_string() usage in mark_sent
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has fundamental architectural violations: primitive obsession (String, bool, u64), missing typestates, no preconditions on transitions, and pub fields exposing internal state. These are BLOCKER-level issues that require structural refactoring, not incremental fixes.
